title: Can you help me?
summary: Ask strangers for help, explain that you have lost something, follow directions to the police station, and put 'me', 'you', 'him' and 'her' on the end of a verb: سَاعِدْنِي (help me).
intro: In the centre of Amman Daniel suddenly can't find his wallet. To ask for help you need object endings on verbs. They are the same endings you know from nouns, with one exception: 'me' is ـنِي on a verb. Compare غُرْفَتِي (my room) with سَاعِدْنِي (help me!) and هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تُسَاعِدَنِي؟ (can you help me?). 'It' is ـهُ for a masculine word and ـهَا for a feminine one, so a lost wallet, مِحْفَظَة, becomes وَجَدْتُهَا (I found it).
objectives: Ask a stranger politely for help: هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تُسَاعِدَنِي؟
Say that you have lost something with ضَاعَ / ضَاعَتْ
Put object endings on verbs: سَاعِدْنِي, أُسَاعِدُكَ, وَجَدْتُهَا
Understand simple directions to the police station

realLife.title: A lost wallet in downtown Amman
realLife.story: After a falafel breakfast and some shopping in the old centre of Amman, Daniel puts his hand in his pocket and finds nothing. A friendly older man tells him what to do, the keffiyeh seller remembers him, and the story ends at the police station next to the big mosque.

sentences.literal: are you able that you help me?

mistakes.why: 'Me' after a verb is the ending -nī, never the word anā.
miḥfaẓa (wallet) is feminine, so the verb takes -at: ḍāʿat.

sentences.en: I found it on the table.
sentences.literal: I found her (= it, the wallet) on the table

mistakes.why: The wallet, miḥfaẓa, is feminine, so 'it' is -hā.

sentences.en: I'm looking for the police station.
sentences.literal: I search about (the) centre (of) the police

dialogue.title: The black wallet
dialogue.culture: The old centre of Amman (people say فِي وَسَطِ الْبَلَد, 'in the middle of town') is full of small shops, falafel restaurants and sweet shops famous for their الْكُنَافَة. People often call an older man يَا عَمّ ('uncle') and a young man يَا ابْنِي ('my son'): it is warm, not rude. In an emergency the number for the police in Jordan is 911.

lines.ar: لَوْ سَمَحْتَ يَا عَمّ، هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تُسَاعِدَنِي؟ عِنْدِي مُشْكِلَة كَبِيرَة.
lines.en: Excuse me, sir, can you help me? I have a big problem.

lines.ar: طَبْعًا يَا ابْنِي، أُسَاعِدُكَ بِكُلِّ سُرُور. مَا الْمُشْكِلَة؟ لَا تَقْلَقْ، وَتَكَلَّمْ بِبُطْء.
lines.en: Of course, son, I'll gladly help you. What's the problem? Don't worry, and speak slowly.

lines.ar: ضَاعَتْ مِحْفَظَتِي! كَانَتْ فِي جَيْبِي قَبْلَ سَاعَة، وَالْآنَ لَا أَجِدُهَا فِي أَيِّ مَكَان.
lines.en: I've lost my wallet! It was in my pocket an hour ago, and now I can't find it anywhere.

lines.ar: أَيْنَ كُنْتَ قَبْلَ سَاعَة؟ وَمَاذَا فَعَلْتَ؟ رُبَّمَا نَسِيتَهَا فِي مَحَلّ أَوْ فِي مَطْعَم.
lines.en: Where were you an hour ago? And what did you do? Maybe you left it in a shop or in a restaurant.
segs: you forgot it (f), you left it (to a man)

lines.ar: أَكَلْتُ فَلَافِل فِي مَطْعَم صَغِير فِي هٰذَا الشَّارِع، ثُمَّ اشْتَرَيْتُ كُوفِيَّة لِأَبِي مِنْ مَحَلّ قَرِيب.
lines.en: I ate falafel in a small restaurant on this street, then I bought a keffiyeh for my father in a shop nearby.

lines.ar: وَدَفَعْتَ فِي الْمَحَلّ نَقْدًا يَا دَانْيَال، أَنَا رَأَيْتُكَ. إِذَنْ كَانَتِ الْمِحْفَظَة مَعَكَ هُنَاكَ.
lines.en: And you paid in cash in the shop, Daniel: I saw you. So the wallet was with you there.

lines.ar: إِذَنِ اذْهَبْ إِلَى الْمَحَلّ أَوَّلًا، وَاسْأَلِ الْبَائِع. وَإِذَا لَمْ تَجِدْهَا هُنَاكَ، فَمَرْكَزُ الشُّرْطَة فِي آخِرِ الشَّارِع.
lines.en: Then go to the shop first and ask the shopkeeper. And if you don't find it there, the police station is at the end of the street.

lines.ar: صَبَاحُ الْخَيْر! اِشْتَرَيْتُ مِنْكَ كُوفِيَّة قَبْلَ سَاعَة. هَلْ رَأَيْتَ مِحْفَظَة سَوْدَاء هُنَا، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ؟
lines.en: Good morning! I bought a keffiyeh from you an hour ago. Did you see a black wallet here, please?

lines.ar: مِحْفَظَة سَوْدَاء؟ نَعَم! وَجَدْتُهَا عَلَى الطَّاوِلَة بَعْدَ أَنْ خَرَجْتَ، فَأَخَذْتُهَا إِلَى مَرْكَزِ الشُّرْطَة قَبْلَ نِصْفِ سَاعَة.
lines.en: A black wallet? Yes! I found it on the counter after you left, so I took it to the police station half an hour ago.
segs: you went out, you left (to a man)

lines.ar: شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا عَلَى الْمُسَاعَدَة! هَلْ تَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ تَقُولَ لِي أَيْنَ مَرْكَزُ الشُّرْطَة بِالضَّبْط؟
lines.en: Thank you so much for your help! Can you tell me exactly where the police station is?

lines.ar: سَهْل جِدًّا: اِمْشِ مُسْتَقِيمًا، ثُمَّ خُذْ أَوَّلَ شَارِع عَلَى الْيَسَار. الْمَرْكَز بِجَانِبِ الْمَسْجِد الْكَبِير.
lines.en: Very easy: walk straight on, then take the first street on the left. The station is next to the big mosque.

lines.ar: أَهْلًا! نَعَم، عِنْدَنَا مِحْفَظَة سَوْدَاء. لٰكِنْ أَوَّلًا: مَا اسْمُكَ؟ وَمَاذَا يُوجَدُ فِي الْمِحْفَظَة؟
lines.en: Hello! Yes, we have a black wallet. But first: what's your name? And what is in the wallet?

lines.ar: اِسْمِي دَانْيَال. فِيهَا بِطَاقَةُ الْبَنْك، وَصُورَة لِأُخْتِي إِيمَا، وَأَرْبَعُونَ دِينَارًا تَقْرِيبًا.
lines.en: My name is Daniel. There's a bank card in it, a photo of my sister Emma, and about forty dinars.

lines.ar: صَحِيح، هٰذِهِ مِحْفَظَتُكَ. تَفَضَّلْ! وَأَرْجُو أَنْ تَضَعَهَا فِي حَقِيبَتِكَ فِي الْمَرَّة الْقَادِمَة.
lines.en: That's right, this is your wallet. Here you are! And please put it in your bag next time.

lines.ar: الْحَمْدُ لِلّٰه! النَّاس هُنَا طَيِّبُونَ جِدًّا: كُلُّ شَخْص سَأَلْنَاهُ الْيَوْمَ سَاعَدَنَا.
lines.en: Thank God! People here are very kind: everyone we asked today helped us.

lines.ar: صَحِيح! شُكْرًا لَكَ يَا حَضْرَةَ الشُّرْطِيّ. وَالْآنَ أَدْعُوكِ يَا لَيْلَى إِلَى الْكُنَافَة… بِمِحْفَظَتِي!
lines.en: True! Thank you, officer. And now, Layla, I'm treating you to kunafa… with my own wallet!

reading.title: A happy ending
reading.ar: فِي وَسَطِ الْبَلَد ضَاعَتْ مِحْفَظَةُ دَانْيَال. سَأَلَ رَجُلًا فِي الشَّارِع، وَالرَّجُل سَاعَدَهُ. وَجَدَ الْبَائِع الْمِحْفَظَة فِي مَحَلِّهِ، وَأَخَذَهَا إِلَى مَرْكَزِ الشُّرْطَة. هُنَاكَ أَعْطَاهَا الشُّرْطِيّ لِدَانْيَال.
reading.en: In the city centre Daniel lost his wallet. He asked a man in the street, and the man helped him. The shopkeeper found the wallet in his shop and took it to the police station. There the policeman gave it to Daniel.

options: the old man in the street

quiz.prompt: Choose the right ending: 'I found it' (the wallet, مِحْفَظَة)
How do you ask a man politely 'Can you help me?'
Which word has ʿayn (ع), the sound from deep in the throat?

completion: Well done! You can ask for help, explain what you have lost and follow directions, and you can put 'me', 'you' and 'it' on the end of a verb. Next time: bigger and smaller.
